event_confirmation: Company release (Business Wire, 2026-10-05, mirrored on Nasdaq and StockTitan): Amkor reports Q3 2026 results on Monday 2026-10-26 AFTER the Nasdaq close, with a call at 5 p.m. ET. Session amc confirmed. https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/amkor-technology-announce-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-october-26-2026-2026
conviction_note: Q4 guidance decides this print, as it did in July (Q2 beat on revenue and margin, weak Q3 revenue guide, stock -24.7%). The only new information on the guide line since July is negative: Apple cut iPhone 18 Pro orders 15-20% (Nikkei, 2026-10-09). The NVIDIA/computing ramp offsets it, and a 31% slide since 2026-10-02 plus +17.6 put skew already prices much of it. So p_up 48 on abs 12 gives -0.48. The positive findings (ASE's Q3 ATM beat, TI, TSMC, Amkor's own beat record) all land on the reported quarter, and this name sells beats. That is why the findings sum (+0.6) and the scaled number (-0.48) have opposite signs.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $2.04B and EPS $0.78-0.79. Two sources agree: GuruFocus preview 2026-10-26 (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9142602/amkor-technology-amkr-set-to-report-q3-earnings-amid-mixed-market-signals) and Benzinga/MarketBeat (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AMKR/earnings-forecasts). That sits at the top of the company guide of $1.95-2.05B revenue, 18.5-19.5% gross margin and $0.72-0.82 EPS (8-K 2026-07-27, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001047127/000104712726000043/amkr6302026erex-991.htm). The Q4 bar is only partly sourced: about $2.05B on a single Benzinga snapshot from about September, so the guidance findings are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 10.66M shares, 5.83% of float, days to cover 3.1, settlement 2026-09-30, published by FINRA 2026-10-09, up 7.7% from the prior report (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/AMKR/short-interest/). Not crowded. Skew_25d is +17.6 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI is 1.11, and Tickeron cites a put/call near 2.38 in early October. The stock is -28.5% over 20 days, -9.3% over 5 days and -59% off its 52-week high of $96.68. The Kim family holds over 49% and insiders 26%, so the float is smaller than shares outstanding. The B. Riley target cut (2026-10-20, $65 to $46, Neutral) expects Q3 and the Q4 guide 'roughly in line with consensus'.

findings.finding: Q4 guide risk from the iPhone. Nikkei (2026-10-09) reports Apple cut October component orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max by at least 15% (15-20% per one executive). Loop Capital (2026-10-21) puts the 2H26 cut at about 13M units and the December-quarter shipments at 79M against 85M. Amkor's Communications line is 42% of sales, and in July management had already guided it down high single digits in Q3, said Q4 would see 'a little bit of softness' and 'no significant H2 lift'. The Q4 revenue consensus of about $2.05B (flat on Q3) was set before the cut. Amkor's own Q4 2025 guide was -8% on Q3 ($1.775-1.875B against $1.99B).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: Q3 revenue guide of $1.95-2.05B against about $2.09B consensus took the stock -24.74% despite a Q2 beat. October 2025: Q4 guided down about 8% QoQ, stock -3.07%. February 2025: weak Q1 and an iOS socket loss, stock -11.33%. Guidance misses have moved this name the most.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The stock went from $55 on Oct 2 (Form 4 sale price) to $46.92 on Oct 13 and $38 today, and the skew pays for downside. Amkor is not named in the Nikkei story. The residual risk is that the Q4 consensus snapshot was not cut to match; B. Riley's 'in line' preview suggests the street expects the computing ramp to cover it. If it were fully priced, the Q4 consensus would sit below Q3 the way it did in 2025.
findings.independence: Loop Capital note via MacRumors, 2026-10-21 (https://macrumors.com/2026/10/21/loop-capital-cuts-apple-rating-over-iphone-sales-outlook). Management's own July commentary on Q4 comms softness (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2939619). Q4 2025 guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1047127/000104712725000187/amkr9302025erex-991.htm). Net of the rest of the company: computing (22% of sales, guided +~30% QoQ in Q3, HDFO CPU and NVIDIA ramps) and auto/industrial (22%) must grow roughly 8-10% QoQ to keep Q4 flat. That is plausible, so this finding is sized net and small.

findings.finding: Peer read-through for the reported quarter. ASE's ATM (assembly, test and materials) revenue for Q3 2026 was NT$151.5B, +20.1% QoQ (+18.7% in USD, +40.6% YoY). In July ASE guided ATM +11-13% QoQ, so the largest OSAT beat its own Q3 guide by about 7-8 points. Amkor's Q3 consensus of $2.04B implies +7.5% QoQ, near the top of its $1.95-2.05B guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue $1.898B against a $1.75-1.85B guide (+2.6% above the top) and gross margin 16.8% against a 14.5-15.5% guide, and the stock fell 24.74% on the guide. This name sells reported-quarter beats.
findings.why_not_priced: ASE's September revenue was public on Oct 12, yet AMKR fell from about $47 to $38 afterward, so the market did not carry the OSAT-strength read across. If it had, the Q3 consensus would sit above the top of guide rather than at it. The caveat is that ASE's beat is heavily AI/CoWoS and SPIL-driven, while Amkor's Q3 has an iOS/Android drag.
findings.independence: ASE's Q3 guide of ATM +11-13% QoQ is from its Q2 results coverage (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/ase-technology-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-30/); that figure comes from one source in the search summary. TSMC's Q3 beat is a separate finding.

findings.finding: Amkor's own guide-beat record. Q2 2026 revenue was $1.898B against a $1.75-1.85B guide, gross margin 16.8% against 14.5-15.5%, EPS $0.70 against $0.42-0.52. Q1 2026 revenue was $1.685B against a $1.65B consensus. Utilization was in the high 70s in Q2, and management said utilization excluding Korea-to-Vietnam transit assets was 'pretty high'. A similar beat would put Q3 at about $2.05-2.10B and gross margin above 19.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 beat was sold (-24.74%) because of the guide. Q1 2026 was a small beat with stock -5.63%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The consensus already sits at the top of guide and the EPS consensus of $0.78-0.79 is near the guide's upper half. Only an above-top beat is unpriced.
findings.independence: The Q1 2026 8-K for the Q2 guide (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001047127/000104712726000017/amkr3312026erex-991.htm). This rests on Amkor's own documents, separate from the ASE finding, although both lean toward a Q3 beat.

findings.finding: Auto/industrial counterparty strength. Texas Instruments reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-21: revenue $6.05-6.06B against $5.91B consensus (+28% YoY, +11% QoQ), analog +32%. Its Q4 guide is $5.80-6.30B (midpoint about flat QoQ, against TI's usual seasonal decline). Amkor's automotive, industrial and other line is 22% of sales and was guided +mid-single digits QoQ in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved Amkor print where auto/industrial alone moved the stock. In February 2025 auto weakness was cited alongside the iOS socket loss (-11.33%).
findings.why_not_priced: TI spoke after Amkor last guided, and AMKR has fallen since with the sector. This is a proxy: TI's own packaging is largely in-house, so transmission to Amkor's auto line is inferred, not confirmed by a direct counterparty.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-21 Amkor announced a new $1.3B multi-year agreement with NVIDIA to expand advanced packaging capacity in South Korea, bringing NVIDIA agreements across Korea and Arizona to $3B. It also plans to raise interposer wafer capacity by more than 300% by end-2028. That gives the call material to support a Computing-led Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July NVIDIA $1.5B Arizona deal (announced 2026-07-23) did not stop the -24.74% post-print move. After the 2026-10-21 Korea deal the stock went from $41.94 (Oct 20) to $39.30 (Oct 23), so the market faded it.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and faded. What remains is whether management quantifies Q4 computing growth or NVIDIA prepayment timing on the call (in July the prepayment was said to arrive in 2027). If it were priced as a growth driver, the stock would not have fallen after the announcement.
findings.independence: July NVIDIA partnership (https://evertiq.com/design/2026-07-24-nvidia-amkor-sign-15-billion-chip-packaging-agreement) and management's July 'computing nearly +30% QoQ' guide (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2939619).

findings.finding: Capex and financing. On 2026-09-08 Amkor expanded its Arizona campus to about $12B (Phase 2, +60,000 m2 cleanroom, construction late 2027 to 2029) 'because customer commitments exceeded Phase 1'. 2026 capex is $2.5-3.0B against H1 PP&E payments of $688M. Capex payable was $621M, and $1.15B of 0% converts were issued in May 2026. Management warned that the US manufacturing burden will weigh on margins in 2027-2028. A 2027 capex or margin framework may appear on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The February 2026 Kim-family secondary (10M shares at $48.75) cost about 6-7% intraday, a different item.
findings.why_not_priced: The spend is public. The answer to 'what does the money buy' is customer commitments (NVIDIA prepayments, Arizona and Korea), so it funds visible demand. The sign is zero, with downside only if a 2027 capex guide lands well above the street.
findings.independence: The CFO's July capex and margin comments (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2939619) and the NVIDIA Korea deal (shares the NVIDIA entity with the finding above; not counted twice).

findings.finding: Much of the October drawdown is sector beta. The SOX had a six-day losing streak worth about $1.6T (Bloomberg, 2026-10-14), and Lam Research's 2026-10-21 call warning of cleanroom and supply constraints into 2027 took SOXX -6% on 2026-10-22. AMKR has a beta of about 2.2 and fell from about $55 (Oct 2) to $38. Part of the 31% is the sector, not a company-specific Q4 problem, so a guide near consensus meets a stock positioned for a miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Two up moves in seven prints, +18.13% (July 2025) and +1.79% (February 2026). The +18% came after a weak period, when guidance cleared the bar.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement about what is priced. The skew and put/call show the market is already braced for a bad guide. If the decline were company-specific, the B. Riley preview would not call Q3 and Q4 in line. Small, because a drawdown is not by itself a reason to bounce.
findings.independence: Bloomberg on the SOX $1T+ loss (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-14/chip-stocks-set-to-erase-1-trillion-in-value-as-rout-deepens) and Tickeron's 30-day decomposition (https://tickeron.com/blogs/amkor-technology-amkr-stock-falls-27-6-in-30-days-key-factors-and-outlook-20708/).

findings.finding: Android and memory headwinds in Communications. In July management cited memory supply constraints and Android revenue down about 20%, and expected continued Android weakness. IDC (via secondary outlets) projects 2026 smartphone units -16.7%, the steepest decline on record. This bears on the Q4 comms guide beyond the iPhone cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same comms line as the iPhone finding. The July guide miss (-24.74%) was partly comms-driven.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: management told the market in July, so this sits inside what the company already guided. The only residual is the worsening memory shortage since then, and the IDC figure comes from a secondary outlet.
findings.independence: IndexBox on memory costs (https://www.indexbox.io/blog/apple-trims-iphone-18-pro-component-orders-as-memory-costs-surge/). Shares the comms line with the iPhone finding but rests on a different customer set (Android).

findings.finding: TSMC's Q3 2026 revenue of about $46.7B beat the high end of its guide. It guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3B (about +14% QoQ at the midpoint) and lists CoWoS and advanced packaging capacity as tight. Digitimes (January 2026) reported TSMC moving some advanced packaging orders to OSATs including Amkor. That supports the AI/2.5D side of Amkor's Computing guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated history. Computing was the bright spot in July and did not offset the comms-driven guide miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since Oct 15 and the stock fell afterward with the sector. The transmission to Amkor's revenue is an inference (proxy), so this is sized small.
findings.independence: TSMC 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001046179/000104617926000726/a3q26e_withguidancexfinal.htm). Shares an AI-demand theme with the ASE finding but is a different document and line.

findings.finding: Insider selling into the slide is small and pre-planned. CFO Megan Faust sold 1,000 shares at $46.92 on 2026-10-13 (10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-02-17, holds 133,105). Director Douglas Alexander exercised and sold 5,000 at $55 on 2026-10-02 (plan adopted 2026-05-08).
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial in size and scheduled under plans adopted months ago, so it carries no information about Q4. Filed for completeness.

outside_window.finding: Apple reports its September quarter after the exit window (about 2026-10-29/30); its December-quarter iPhone commentary would re-rate Amkor's comms exposure only after the trade closes.
Arizona Phase 2 construction (late 2027 to 2029) and the 2028 Arizona margin burden flagged by the CFO are multi-year items beyond the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Current Q4 2026 revenue consensus from a dated source after the iPhone cut (only a Benzinga snapshot from about September, $2.05B)
A direct Apple-supplier read-through naming Amkor in the October iPhone 18 Pro cut reports (Amkor not named by Nikkei)
Nasdaq short-interest API (503); used the MarketBeat FINRA mirror instead
Any Amkor 8-K between the July print and today beyond the ordinary press releases; EDGAR shows only Form 4 and Form 144 filings since August
Full July call Q&A on Q4 iOS share or socket changes (transcript partial)

rejected_candidates.candidate: KeyBanc target cut $34 to $27 citing an iOS socket loss and auto weakness
rejected_candidates.detail: The note is dated 2025-02-12 (page metadata), not October 2026. It is a stale story served with a current-looking page, so it has no bearing on this print.
The headline percentages contradict the article's own price data ($49.12, -3.69%) and give no cause; the drawdown is already covered by the sector and iPhone findings.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Kim family secondary of 10M shares at $48.75 (Feb 2026), 180-day lock-up expired about 2026-08-11; GuruFocus says insiders sold $992M over 12 months
rejected_candidates.detail: No Form 144 or 4 since the lock-up ended shows a Kim-family sale; EDGAR's August-October Form 4 list shows small officer and director plan sales only, so no overhang evidence for the window. The GuruFocus figure is internally inconsistent.

baseline_tension: The evidence mostly agrees with the skew and the run-up. The one new negative (the iPhone cut) is what the 31% October slide and the +17.6 put skew already price. The positives are reported-quarter items this name sells, so nothing here beats the baseline decisively and p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the ASE peer beat went from +1.0 to +0.6 and Amkor's own beat record from +0.4 to +0.2, because this name sold a strong Q2 beat (-24.7%).
Lessons 6 and 9 (bar; net of segment): the iPhone/Q4 guide finding went from -1.5 to -1.0. The Q4 bar rests on one stale snapshot, and computing and auto (44% of sales) can offset comms.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the Arizona capex finding went from -0.3 to 0.0, because the spend is backed by customer commitments and NVIDIA prepayments.

Lesson 5 (proxies small; inside the company's guide): the Android/memory finding went from -0.5 to -0.2 (management guided it in July), and TI and TSMC went from +0.4 to +0.3 each as unconfirmed transmission.
Lessons 5 and 7 (a drawdown is not a cause): the sector-beta positioning finding went from +0.5 to +0.2.
Unchanged: p_up 48, insider and NVIDIA findings (NVIDIA +0.3 to +0.2 as faded news). abs_move went from 11 to 12 because the Q4 guide is the deciding line and recent guide reactions were 11-25%.
